doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Hearing John play George Barnes's arrangement
summary: Rowe plays a recording in which John Pizzarelli uses Barnes's arrangement and a banjo-derived wrist technique learned from the uncles.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: That’s 53 years of playing the guitar.
Well I have something I wanted to play for you.
Oh that’s John [Pizzarelli Junior]. Well he got that from George.
He got that from George? This is wild. That was great how it came out of that.
Yeah. We got that from George. In fact we sent his widow a copy of this.
It almost sounds like you guys had played some banjo along the way too.
Well that’s what it’s from. You know John studied banjo with my uncles, and they had this wrist thing going, so you apply it to guitar, that’s what happens.
